proposal.summary: Tutor LMS WordPress plugin versions 1.5.2 and below contain CSRF vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to cause an admin to approve or block instructors via crafted GET requests and to add instructor accounts via CSRF on admin POST endpoints, enabling attacker-controlled instructor creation or blocking of legitimate instructors.
proposal.affected_product: Tutor LMS WordPress plugin, version 1.5.2 and below
proposal.cwe_quote: An attacker can use CSRF to register themselves as an instructor or block other legit instructors.

AV.quote: As the requests for the approval and blocking of instructors are sent using the GET method, the CSRF attack to approve an attacker-controlled instructor account can be performed by having the admin visit https://TARGET/wp-admin/admin.php?page=tutor-instructors&action=approve&instructor=8 directly,

PR.quote: an admin who is logged in at https://TARGET can be tricked into visiting the link and triggering the request to add an instructor.

UI.quote: an admin who is logged in at https://TARGET can be tricked into visiting the link and triggering the request to add an instructor.

C.quote: An attacker can use CSRF to register themselves as an instructor or block other legit instructors.

I.quote: An attacker can use CSRF to register themselves as an instructor or block other legit instructors.

A.quote: An attacker can use CSRF to register themselves as an instructor or block other legit instructors.

proposal.recommended_next_step: Verify the plugin version on affected sites, confirm the presence of CSRF protections (nonces) on the described endpoints, and apply the vendor patch (Tutor LMS 1.5.3) or implement CSRF token checks and change state-modifying actions to require POST with valid nonces.

evidence_quotes.quote: All WordPress websites using Tutor LMS version 1.5.2 and below are affected.

evidence_quotes.claim: CSRF allows registering as instructor or blocking instructors
evidence_quotes.quote: An attacker can use CSRF to register themselves as an instructor or block other legit instructors.

evidence_quotes.claim: State-modifying actions use GET allowing CSRF via link click
evidence_quotes.quote: As the requests for the approval and blocking of instructors are sent using the GET method, the CSRF attack to approve an attacker-controlled instructor account can be performed by having the admin visit https://TARGET/wp-admin/admin.php?page=tutor-instructors&action=approve&instructor=8 directly,

evidence_quotes.claim: CSRF via POST form to add instructor
evidence_quotes.quote: CSRF attack can also be performed on the form present at https://TARGET/wp-admin/admin.php?page=tutor-instructors&sub_page=add_new_instructor in order to have the admin add an instructor account for the attacker, thus bypassing the requirement for approval.
Tutor LMS version 1.5.3 containing the fix released – February 4, 2020.
